svg.text: Immunity: two questions decide every exam item
Question 1 — WHO made the antibody?
The patient did = ACTIVE. Somebody else did and it was given = PASSIVE.
ACTIVE — the body makes it
SLOW to develop — days to weeks
LONG lasting — often for life
Memory cells are formed
Natural: having had measles
Artificial: measles VACCINE
Slow to arrive, stays for years.
Use it to PREVENT, before exposure.
PASSIVE — antibody is handed over
IMMEDIATE protection
SHORT lived — weeks to months
NO memory cells formed
Natural: mother to baby, placenta and
breast milk
Artificial: tetanus immunoglobulin
Instant, but it fades and is gone.
Question 2 — was it given on purpose?
Nature did it = NATURAL. A clinician did it = ARTIFICIAL. The two questions give four boxes.
The deep wound with no tetanus cover
Give BOTH: immunoglobulin for protection
NOW, and vaccine for protection LATER.
Passive covers the gap while active develops.
Herd immunity
When enough people are immune the organism
cannot find a chain of susceptible hosts.
It protects the newborn and the immunosuppressed,
